questions.prompt: Why is timely patching one of the highest-value security controls?

options.text: Attackers quickly weaponize known vulnerabilities and scan for unpatched systems
It removes the need for backups
Only patched systems can use encryption

questions.explanation: Most attacks reuse publicly known vulnerabilities and scan the internet for unpatched systems, so prompt patching removes the exact doors they use.

questions.prompt: Encrypting a laptop's storage so a lost or stolen device stays confidential is called full-disk ____.
questions.explanation: Full-disk encryption (BitLocker, FileVault, LUKS) protects data at rest, so device theft doesn't become a data breach.

questions.prompt: Match each hardening action to what it reduces.

pairs.right: Risk of data loss on device theft

questions.explanation: Each hardening step targets a specific weakness: fewer services, less privilege, secure baselines, and protected data at rest.

questions.prompt: Which are good endpoint-hardening practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Automate security updates and prioritize internet-facing systems
Use standard accounts for daily work and elevate per action
Remove default credentials and unused services
Make every user a local administrator for convenience

questions.explanation: Automated updates, least-privilege accounts, and removing defaults/unused services harden endpoints; making everyone admin maximizes blast radius.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to harden a new internet-facing server.

items.text: Disable unused services and close unneeded ports
Set up least-privilege accounts (no shared admin)
Apply a hardening baseline and enable the host firewall

questions.explanation: Patch first, reduce attack surface, tighten accounts, then apply a secure baseline and firewall — each step removes exposure or caps damage.

questions.prompt: Why should daily work use a standard (non-admin) account?

options.text: If malware runs, it inherits only limited rights, capping the damage
It disables the need for patching

questions.explanation: Running as a standard user means malware executing in that context inherits limited privileges, greatly reducing what it can do compared with admin.
